creator: wokweekly
title: Dan Dan Noodles
description: Sauce in the bowl, noodles on top, mix at the table. The sesame paste has to be loosened first or it seizes.
steps: Loosen the sesame paste with 3 tbsp of warm water, a spoonful at a time, until it pours.
Stir in the soy, vinegar, chilli oil and Sichuan pepper and divide between two bowls.
Fry the pork in a dry hot wok for 5 minutes, until dark brown and crisp at the edges and cooked through.
Add the mustard greens and fry for 1 minute more.
Boil the noodles per the packet and lift them straight onto the sauce.
Top with the pork and spring onion. Mix hard before eating.

creator: wokweekly
title: Pad Krapow Moo
description: Holy basil, not sweet basil, and a fried egg on top. Twelve minutes start to finish.
steps: Fry the eggs in 2 tbsp of very hot oil until the edges are crisp and brown. Set aside.
Add the garlic and chilli to the wok and fry for 20 seconds.
Add the pork and fry hard for 5 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and cooked through.
Add the oyster sauce, fish sauce and sugar with a splash of water and toss for 1 minute.
Kill the heat and stir the basil through until it just wilts.
Serve over rice with the egg on top.

creator: wokweekly
title: Bibimbap
description: Everything cooked separately, arranged in sections, then destroyed at the table.
steps: Season the blanched spinach and sprouts separately with sesame oil, a little garlic and salt.
Stir-fry the courgette for 2 minutes and the carrot for 3, keeping them separate.
Fry the eggs so the yolks stay runny.
Put the hot rice in bowls and arrange each vegetable in its own section on top.
Add the egg in the middle and a spoon of gochujang beside it.
Scatter with sesame seeds and mix everything together before eating.

creator: wokweekly
title: Char Siu Pork
description: Two days if you can — one to marinate, one to roast. The last five minutes under the grill make the edges.
steps: Mix everything except half the honey and rub it into the pork.
Marinate in the fridge for at least 8 hours, ideally 24.
Heat the oven to 190C. Sit the pork on a rack over a tray of water so the drips do not smoke.
Roast for 25 minutes, turn, and roast 25 minutes more.
Brush with the reserved honey and grill on high for 5 minutes, until the edges char and blister.
Rest for 10 minutes, then slice across the strips.

creator: wokweekly
title: Quick Miso Ramen
description: Not a twelve-hour broth, and it does not pretend to be. Forty minutes and it still tastes like something.
steps: Fry the pork in the sesame oil over high heat for 4 minutes, until browned and cooked through.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Whisk the miso with a ladle of the stock until smooth, then add it and the rest of the stock.
Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Do not let it boil hard or the miso goes grainy.
Cook the noodles separately and divide between bowls.
Pour over the broth and top with egg, corn and spring onion.

creator: wokweekly
title: Pork and Cabbage Gyoza
description: Fry, steam, fry again. The third stage is what gives you the crisp bottom.
steps: Salt the cabbage and leave it 15 minutes, then squeeze it dry in a cloth. Wet filling makes the wrappers split.
Mix the cabbage with the pork, garlic, ginger, soy and sesame oil.
Put a teaspoon in each wrapper, wet the edge, and pleat one side onto the other.
Fry flat side down in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, until the bottoms are golden.
Add 100ml water and cover immediately. Steam for 6 minutes until the water has gone.
Uncover and fry for 2 minutes more to re-crisp the base. The pork should be cooked through.
Lift out bottom side up.

creator: wokweekly
title: Beef Rendang
description: Cook it until the sauce disappears into the meat. If it is still saucy it is a curry, not a rendang.
steps: Blend the shallots, garlic, chillies and galangal to a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the paste in a dry heavy pot over medium heat for 8 minutes, until it darkens and smells sweet rather than raw.
Add the ground spices and cook for 1 minute.
Add the beef, coconut milk, lemongrass and lime leaves and bring to a bare simmer.
Cook uncovered for 3 hours, stirring more often as it thickens, until the liquid has gone and the oil has separated.
Keep stirring for the last 15 minutes so the meat fries in its own oil and darkens.

creator: wokweekly
title: Hainanese Chicken Rice
description: The rice is cooked in the poaching liquid. That is the whole dish; the chicken is almost incidental.
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the spring onions and ginger and cover with water.
Bring to a bare simmer, then cook for 35 minutes with the lid on — the water should never boil.
Check the thigh: the juices must run clear and a probe should read 74C.
Lift the chicken into iced water for 5 minutes to firm the skin, then rest it.
Fry the garlic in the chicken fat for 1 minute, add the rice, and turn it for 2 minutes.
Add 3 cups of the poaching broth, cover, and cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then rest 10.
Joint the chicken and serve over the rice with cucumber and soy.

creator: wokweekly
title: Tom Kha Gai
description: Coconut, galangal and lime. Never let it boil hard or the coconut milk splits.
steps: Bring the stock, galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves to a simmer and infuse for 10 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and keep it at a bare tremble — a hard boil will split it.
Add the chicken and mushrooms and poach for 8 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Take it off the heat before seasoning with the fish sauce and lime juice.
Scatter with coriander.

creator: wokweekly
title: Chicken Banh Mi
description: The pickle needs thirty minutes minimum. Everything else takes ten.
steps: Mix the vinegar, sugar and 1 tsp salt with 1/4 cup water and submerge the carrot and daikon. Leave 30 minutes.
Marinate the chicken in the fish sauce for 10 minutes.
Fry over medium-high heat for 5 minutes a side, until charred at the edges and cooked through, then slice.
Hollow the baguettes slightly and spread with mayonnaise.
Fill with chicken, drained pickles, cucumber and coriander.

creator: wokweekly
title: Japchae
description: Dress the noodles while warm and cook every vegetable separately. It takes longer and it matters.
steps: Boil the noodles for 7 minutes, drain, and cut them a few times with scissors.
Dress them straight away with half the soy, sesame oil and sugar while still hot.
Stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes, the carrot for 3 and the mushrooms for 4 — each on its own, each seasoned lightly.
Squeeze the blanched spinach dry and season it with sesame oil.
Toss everything through the noodles with the rest of the soy and sugar.
Finish with sesame seeds. Eat warm or at room temperature.

creator: wokweekly
title: Mapo Aubergine
description: The vegetarian cousin. Salt the aubergine or it drinks the entire bottle of oil.
steps: Salt the aubergine and leave it in a colander for 20 minutes, then pat it dry.
Fry it in the oil over high heat for 6 minutes, until browned and collapsing.
Push it aside, add the doubanjiang and fry for 1 minute until the oil reddens.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then the stock.
Simmer for 5 minutes, add the slurry, and cook 1 minute until glossy.
Off the heat, add the Sichuan pepper and spring onions.

creator: wokweekly
title: Okonomiyaki
description: A cabbage pancake that holds together on faith and one egg. Do not press it down.
steps: Whisk the flour, eggs and dashi to a thick batter and rest it 10 minutes.
Fold in the cabbage and spring onion — it should look like far too much cabbage for the batter.
Heat a frying pan over medium and pile half the mixture in, shaping it into a round about 2cm thick.
Lay two rashers on top and cook for 6 minutes without pressing.
Flip carefully and cook 6 minutes more, until the bacon is crisp and a skewer comes out clean.
Zigzag with sauce and mayonnaise and top with bonito flakes.

creator: wokweekly
title: Prawn Laksa
description: Fry the paste properly first. Everything after that is ten minutes of assembly.
steps: Fry the laksa paste in a little oil over medium heat for 5 minutes, until it darkens and the oil separates.
Add the stock and bring to a simmer for 10 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk and heat gently without boiling.
Add the tofu puffs and simmer 5 minutes, then the prawns for 3 minutes, until pink and opaque throughout.
Season with the fish sauce.
Divide the noodles and sprouts between bowls and ladle the soup over. Serve with lime and coriander.

creator: wokweekly
title: Kung Pao Chicken
description: Velvet the chicken in cornflour first. It is the difference between tender and dry.
steps: Toss the chicken with the cornflour, 1 tbsp soy and a splash of water. Leave 15 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy, vinegar and sugar into a sauce.
Get the wok smoking, add oil, and fry the chillies and peppercorns for 20 seconds.
Add the chicken in one layer and leave it 2 minutes before tossing. Cook 4 minutes total, until cooked through.
Add the garlic and white spring onion for 30 seconds.
Pour in the sauce, toss for 1 minute until it clings, then add the peanuts and green onion off the heat.

creator: wokweekly
title: Pineapple Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice, high heat, and the pineapple added last so it does not turn to mush.
steps: Break the cold rice apart with your hands.
Toast the cashews in the dry wok for 2 minutes and set aside.
Heat the oil until smoking, scramble the eggs quickly and push them aside.
Add the garlic for 20 seconds, then the rice, and fry hard for 4 minutes until it starts to pop.
Season with the fish sauce and curry powder.
Fold in the pineapple, cashews and spring onion for 1 minute only.

creator: wokweekly
title: Beef Bulgogi
description: Grated pear in the marinade tenderises it. Cook it hot and fast in batches or it stews.
steps: Mix the pear, soy, sugar, sesame oil and garlic and marinate the beef for at least 30 minutes.
Get a heavy pan or griddle as hot as it goes.
Cook the beef in a single layer in batches, 90 seconds a side, until caramelised at the edges.
Do not crowd the pan — beef that stews in its marinade goes grey.
Scatter with spring onion and sesame seeds.

creator: wokweekly
title: Ginger Chicken Congee
description: An hour of nearly nothing. Stir it now and then and it goes silky on its own.
steps: Bring the rice, stock and half the ginger to the boil, then drop to the lowest heat.
Cook uncovered for 45 minutes, stirring every 10, until the grains have broken down.
Add the chicken breasts whole and poach for 20 minutes, until cooked through with no pink.
Lift the chicken out, shred it, and stir it back in.
Loosen with more stock if it has gone past thick.
Top with the rest of the ginger, spring onion, sesame oil, soy and crispy shallots.

creator: wokweekly
title: Smashed Cucumber Salad
description: Smash them rather than slice them. The rough edges hold the dressing.
steps: Lay the cucumbers on a board and hit them with the flat of a heavy knife until they split.
Tear them into rough pieces and toss with the salt. Leave 15 minutes.
Drain off the water that comes out — this is what stops it going watery on the plate.
Mix the vinegar, soy, sesame oil, garlic and chilli oil.
Toss through and scatter with sesame seeds. Eat within the hour.

creator: wokweekly
title: Mango Sticky Rice
description: Soak the rice overnight and steam it, do not boil it. Boiled glutinous rice is glue.
steps: Drain the soaked rice and steam it over boiling water for 25 minutes, until translucent and tender.
Warm three quarters of the coconut milk with the sugar and salt until dissolved — do not boil.
Pour it over the hot rice, stir once, cover, and leave 20 minutes for it to absorb.
Reduce the remaining coconut milk with a pinch of salt for 3 minutes until thick.
Serve the rice with the mango alongside, the thickened milk poured over, and sesame seeds on top.
